dish: Butter chicken, fish curry and tandoori from the clay oven
address: Balestier Plaza, 400 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
w: A long-running North Indian kitchen in Balestier Plaza — butter chicken, fish curry, naan from the tandoor — that NHB's Balestier Food Trail lists among the road's food institutions and Eatbook names in its Balestier guide.

dish: Teochew peppery clear-soup bak kut teh
n: Kai Juan (Ah Hak) Bak Kut Teh
address: Kai Juan Coffeeshop, 395/397 Balestier Road, Singapore (exact unit to confirm at geocode)
w: Half a century of Teochew-style bak kut teh — a clear, moderately peppery broth over pork ribs, with rice and salted vegetables for about $7.50 — in a coffeeshop of rusty gates, granite floors and wooden tables that still looks 1970s. A stop on NHB's Balestier Food Trail.

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-67, Singapore 320090
w: Whampoa's nasi lemak stall, named in Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls and HungryGoWhere's Whampoa Food Centre guide (a 'Hi Leskmi Whampoa Nasi Lemak' branch also trades at One Punggol).

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-28, Singapore 320091
w: Min jiang kueh, the folded griddle pancake, as a Whampoa breakfast stop — on Daniel Food Diary's 10 Whampoa breakfast stalls and Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls.

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-10, Singapore 320091
w: An early-morning steamed dim sum stall, headlined in Daniel Food Diary's Whampoa breakfast guide and listed in Eatbook's Whampoa Market round-up.

dish: Hand-pulled la mian and xiao long bao
n: Yu Chu La Mian Xiao Long Bao (Whampoa)
address: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-45, Singapore 320091
w: Hand-pulled noodles and soup dumplings made at the stall — HungryGoWhere's Whampoa pick, also in Eatbook's Whampoa Market list.

dish: Bak chor mee soup — yellow-bean, pork-bone and ikan bilis broth with minced meat and pork liver
address: Balestier Road, Singapore (coffeeshop + unit to confirm at geocode)
w: A soup-style bak chor mee built on a broth of yellow beans, pork bones and ikan bilis, loaded with minced meat, mushrooms and slices of pork liver — written up by Miss Tam Chiak and SG Food on Foot.

dish: Signature lor mee with deep-fried cod fish
w: The Balestier branch of the famous Old Airport Road lor mee, with an extended menu: thick starchy gravy over flat noodles, topped with deep-fried cod nuggets ($10 signature) — in Eatbook's Balestier guide and reviewed by Live2Makan.

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-21, Singapore 320091
w: Yong tau foo served in laksa gravy (about $4) — a Whampoa crossover named by City Nomads, TheSmartLocal and Seth Lui.

dish: Deep-fried carrot cake (fried radish cake cubes)
address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-36, Singapore (block to confirm)
w: A morning-only stall (about 6.30am to 12.30pm, Tue-Sun) deep-frying radish cake until crisp outside and soft within — in City Nomads', Eatbook's, TheSmartLocal's and HungryGoWhere's Whampoa guides. Its owner Mr Lim has sold carrot cake in stick form for over two decades (Women's Weekly).

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore (unit to confirm)
w: Whampoa's mee siam specialist — on both Eatbook's 25 Whampoa Market stalls and HungryGoWhere's 15 can't-miss Whampoa stalls.

address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore (unit to confirm)
w: Shaved ice, pandan jelly, coconut milk and gula Melaka — the Whampoa chendol named by both Eatbook and HungryGoWhere.

dish: Traditional loaves and old-school buns baked the old way
address: Balestier, Singapore (street address to confirm at geocode)
w: One of the last Singapore bakeries still making bread the traditional way — old machinery, hand-cut 'blackhead' loaves — and a supplier of bread to kaya-toast chains including Killiney Kopitiam (Eatbook). A stop on NHB's Balestier Food Trail.

dish: Wok-hei Hokkien mee and homemade kaya butter toast
address: Balestier Plaza (level 2), 400 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm)
w: The viral hole-in-the-wall on Balestier Plaza's second floor: wok-kissed Hokkien mee and homemade kaya toast that Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost: 'local breakfast done right') and Miss Tam Chiak have all written up — it has since spawned outlets in Holland Village (Jun 2025) and Fortune Centre (Dec 2025).

dish: Handmade pau (char siew bao, big pau)
w: The cult handmade-bun family business, at its Balestier outlet — Time Out went inside to see how 'Singapore's best handmade buns' are made, and HungryGoWhere interviewed the family on the dying art of handmade baos.

dish: Nanyang-roasted kopi powder (Legacy Blend, roasted with sugar and margarine)
w: A family coffee roaster since 1950 selling Nanyang-style kopi powder — beans from Indonesia roasted the traditional way with sugar and margarine (the Legacy Blend keeps the founding recipe). On NHB's Balestier Food Trail; Makansutra profiled its revival.

dish: Prawn noodle soup (hae mee) with optional pork ribs
n: Ah Hui Big Prawn Noodle (Balestier Food Centre)
address: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-13, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
w: Aromatic, umami-rich prawn noodle soup — a slightly sweet, garlicky prawn stock, firm big prawns and optional tender pork ribs ($5) — the headline stall of Balestier's heritage market building in both Seth Lui's and Women's Weekly's Balestier Food Centre guides.

n: Soon Kee Long House Boneless Duck Rice (Balestier Food Centre)
address: Balestier Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
w: Teochew braised duck rice ($5.50) under thick slabs of boneless duck, cucumber, boiled peanuts and a fragrant braising sauce — picked by Seth Lui and Women's Weekly at Balestier Food Centre.

dish: Popiah and 'eggy, crispy' fried carrot cake
n: Miao Sin Popiah & Carrot Cake — CLOSED
address: Balestier Market & Food Centre, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930
w: CLOSED 26 Feb 2026. Ong Chin Quay's 45-year-old popiah and carrot-cake stall (started 1980 on Upper Boon Keng Road, at Balestier Market since the 2010s) shut when the 72-year-old hawker found no successor (Mothership; Seth Lui). Women's Weekly had named it among Balestier Food Centre's best and Singapore's great popiah stops. Kept here, flagged, as part of the market's record.
